newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Late profit-taking erases Taiwan push over 9,000.
newsitem.headline: Late profit-taking erases Taiwan push over 9,000.

text.p: Late-session profit taking erased a bold push above 9,000 by Taiwan's weighted stock index, with prices turning lower in late trade, brokers said.
Shortly before the close, the index stood at 8,851.11, a slide of 31.02 points or 0.35 percent compared with Friday's finish of 8,882.13.
Turnover was heavy at T$178 billion.

Share prices had rocketed to a sharply higher open, with the rejuvenated index piercing the 9,000 point threshold to hit an intraday high 9,021.87 on strong momentum from a two-week run of seven-year record highs, brokers said.
Brokers had cautioned that profit-taking pressure was likely in Saturday's shortened session.

"The index is at a very high point right now, and no matter how bullish the general sentiment, the market is bound to take a breather at some point," said Oliver Fang, senior analyst for National Securities.
